## Itinerary

### Day 1 – Thu Aug 27
- Chicago ORD → Madrid (Iberia IB 342, Business, dep 4:55 pm, arr Aug 28 8:20 am)

### Day 2 – Fri Aug 28
- 08:20 — Arrive Madrid Barajas T4.
- 10:32 — Depart Madrid–Puerta de Atocha (ALVIA, Localizador **YNPLW2**) → Pamplona/Iruña.
- Transfer Pamplona → Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port (taxi/bus — see Trip References for Taxi Asier contact).
- Check-in: **Gîte de la Porte Saint Jacques** (Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port).
- Pick up pilgrim credential in SJPP if not already obtained.

::: {.callout-note}
Notes — Aug 28
:::

### Day 3 – Sat Aug 29 (Camino Day 1)
- **Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port → Roncesvalles** (~25 km / 15.5 mi) — the Napoleon Route over the Pyrenees.
- Show QR code / passport at check-in. Albergue closes at 22:00; reservation held until 19:00 unless later arrival is flagged.
- Dinner seating 20:30.
- Overnight: **Albergue de Peregrinos de Orreaga-Roncesvalles** (Localizador **AL08344890**).

::: {.callout-caution}
**This is the hardest and most exposed day of the entire Camino** (~1,200 m climb, few bailout points), done one day after a transatlantic flight and jet lag. Start at first light. Check weather the night before — in fog, high wind, or rain, take the lower **Valcarlos route** instead (~19 km, road-based, far less exposure); ask at the SJPP pilgrim office. Carry rain layer, poles, and food/water since services on the Napoleon route are minimal.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Notes — Aug 29
:::

### Days 4–14 – Aug 30 to Sep 9 (Camino Francés – Roncesvalles to Burgos)

::: {.callout-warning}
**Tentative pacing.** Lodging is only confirmed through Roncesvalles (Aug 29). The stages below are the standard Brierley-guide split — a well-tested ~20–25 km/day plan most SJPP pilgrims use, ending in Burgos on Day 12 of walking. It has **zero rest days**, so there's no built-in slack for blisters, heat, or a slow day. If you fall behind pace, the recommended fix is to bus/taxi the final short stretch into Burgos rather than compress a rest day elsewhere — Burgos's train connection to Madrid on Sep 10 is the hard constraint, not any individual stage. Book lodging a day or two ahead given peak-season demand, and adjust freely once on the trail.
:::

- **Day 4 (Aug 30):** Roncesvalles → Zubiri (~21.5 km / 13.4 mi)
- **Day 5 (Aug 31):** Zubiri → Pamplona (~20.4 km / 12.7 mi)
- **Day 6 (Sep 1):** Pamplona → Puente la Reina (~23.8 km / 14.8 mi)
- **Day 7 (Sep 2):** Puente la Reina → Estella (~21.5 km / 13.4 mi)
- **Day 8 (Sep 3):** Estella → Los Arcos (~21.3 km / 13.2 mi)
- **Day 9 (Sep 4):** Los Arcos → Logroño (~27.5 km / 17.1 mi) — long and largely shadeless through vineyard country; start at dawn.
- **Day 10 (Sep 5):** Logroño → Nájera (~29 km / 18.0 mi) — longest stage of the trip, same exposed terrain; start at dawn, carry extra water.
- **Day 11 (Sep 6):** Nájera → Santo Domingo de la Calzada (~21 km / 13.0 mi)
- **Day 12 (Sep 7):** Santo Domingo de la Calzada → Belorado (~22.8 km / 14.2 mi)
- **Day 13 (Sep 8):** Belorado → San Juan de Ortega (~23.7 km / 14.7 mi)
- **Day 14 (Sep 9):** San Juan de Ortega → Burgos (~25.8 km / 16.0 mi)

::: {.callout-note}
Notes — Camino days (add day-by-day as the trip happens)
:::

## Packing List

### Documents & Money
- Passport
- Pilgrim credential (credencial) — get stamped daily
- Pilgrim Pass QR code (register before departure, see note above)
- Flight, train & lodging confirmations (digital copies on phone)
- Credit + ATM cards
- Euro cash (small bills for albergues, donativos)

### Pack Setup
- Backpack with rain cover (35–40L)
- 1 small dry sack (electronics/passport)
- Packing cubes + plastic bags (organization, laundry separation)

### Clothing
- 2 quick-dry short-sleeve tees
- 1 long-sleeve thermal / light layer (cool mornings crossing the Pyrenees on Day 1)
- 1 light fleece or packable insulated layer
- 1 lightweight rain jacket
- 1 convertible hiking pant
- 1 pair town/casual pants or shorts
- 3 pairs quick-dry underwear
- 3 pairs hiking socks (merino blend)

### Footwear
- Trail runners or light hiking shoes (broken in well before the trip)
- Lightweight sandals or flip-flops (evenings)

### Toiletries
- Toothbrush + travel toothpaste
- Small liquid soap (body + laundry, e.g. Dr. Bronner's)
- Travel deodorant
- Quick-dry towel
- Sunscreen (August sun is strong, especially crossing the Meseta near Burgos)
- Lip balm with SPF

### Health & First Aid
- Blister pads (Compeed-style hydrocolloid) — essential for Day 1's Pyrenees crossing
- Ibuprofen / acetaminophen / personal medications
- Hand sanitizer, tissues
- Earplugs + eye mask (shared albergue dorms)
- Trekking poles (recommended for the SJPP–Roncesvalles descent)

### Electronics
- iPhone + USB-C cord
- EU plug adapter
- AirPods
- Portable power bank

### Other
- Sunglasses
- Sun hat
- Sleep sack / liner (albergue bedding varies)
- 2 × 1L water bottles (heat + climb on Day 1 demand real hydration capacity)
- Pen (credencial stamps, customs form on the flight home)
